finding: Unpredictable variable rewards sustain play far longer than predictable ones
label: Established (lab evidence)

finding: Near-misses feel like almost-wins and pull players onward - a mechanic borrowed from gambling
label: Established

finding: Flow - challenge matched to growing skill - is the core engagement state
label: Established

finding: Autonomy, competence and relatedness (self-determination) predict sustained, healthy play
label: Established

finding: Unfinished goals nag at players: visible incomplete quests pull people back (Zeigarnik effect)
label: Established + applied

finding: Curiosity is an information gap: show players something is missing and they will want to close it
label: Established

finding: Over-using extrinsic rewards can hollow out intrinsic motivation - reward the playing, not just the outcome
label: Established (meta-analysis)

finding: Achievements and badges measurably lift activity as a cheap second progression layer
label: Established (field experiment)

finding: Harmonious passion (play fits life) vs obsessive passion (play controls life): design for the first
label: Established

finding: Dopamine tracks novelty and reward prediction, not just reward - a steady drip of new content sustains engagement
label: Established

finding: Absorbing visuospatial play measurably occupies the mind (Tetris intrusion studies) - deep engagement is real but bounded
label: Established (replicated)

finding: Sound is felt as part of the reward: win sounds raise arousal and can distort win perception
label: Established (lab)

finding: Adaptive music that follows game tension significantly raises felt tension and immersion
label: Established (experiment)

finding: Instant audio on every input makes controls feel responsive - sound marks registration before visuals can
label: Established (experiment)

finding: Character-specific sounds improve immersion, avatar identification and fun
label: Established (experiment)

finding: Color shifts emotion: red reads as high-arousal danger, yellow as positive - strongest on new players
label: Established (experiment)

finding: Color is an information channel first: team coding, threat colors, silhouettes (Valve) - readability beats decoration
label: Industry + research

finding: Saturation and brightness are the main mood dials; grading/LUTs tune mood cheaply
label: Industry

finding: Meet contrast and readability standards - clearer for low-vision players and for everyone
label: Accessibility guideline

finding: Juice - screen shake, hit-stop, particles, tweens - makes identical mechanics feel dramatically better
label: Industry consensus

finding: Animation principles (anticipation, squash-and-stretch) keep actions readable and attacks fair
label: Industry craft

finding: VFX should communicate state and guide attention, not just decorate
label: Research + industry

finding: Even simple 2D games measurably gain engagement from layered visual effects
label: Established (experiment)

finding: The compulsion loop (action - reward - new goal) is the engine of one-more-go; keep it fair and completable
label: Industry

finding: Short runs plus a persistent high score drive endless replay
label: Industry + arcade data

finding: Difficulty walls frustrate: easier progression can raise engagement and spending
label: Research brief

finding: Mobile retention is brutal: median D1 about 22%, D7 about 4% - top performers roughly double it
label: Industry benchmark data

finding: Leaderboards motivate via competence: personal-best and near-rank framing beats global bottom ranks
label: Established (experiment)

finding: Re-engagement (notifications, dailies) is a tuned system - Duolingo optimizes it with bandit algorithms
label: Established (deployed ML)

finding: The exploitative line: features that remove stopping cues or manufacture obligation (endless pulls, FOMO, pay-to-skip)
label: Established (reviews/taxonomies)

finding: Engagement is not addiction: the clinical line for gaming disorder is functional impairment (ICD-11), and experts warn against pathologizing normal play
label: Expert consensus

finding: Limited-time FOMO content backfires - it exhausts players and punishes absence
label: Industry observation

finding: Design games you'd thank for the time: gratification (earned satisfaction) over compensation (escape)
label: Research + ethics
